ai.subject: Pathology
ai.summary: Tissue repair is the coordinated cellular and molecular response that restores integrity after injury. It involves inflammation, proliferation, and remodeling, each stage driven by cytokines, growth factors, and extracellular matrix changes.

sections.p: Tissue repair refers to the biological processes that restore damaged tissue structure and function. Diagnosis is clinical, supported by histology or imaging showing granulation tissue, collagen deposition, and scar formation.
Repair is staged into inflammation, proliferation, and remodeling. Severity is judged by extent of tissue loss, infection, and systemic involvement.
Common causes include mechanical injury, infection, ischemia, and systemic conditions. In low‑resource settings, infections (TB, HIV, malaria), malnutrition, and herbal remedies often delay healing.
Patients present with pain, erythema, edema, purulent drainage, or delayed closure. Systemic signs may include fever or malaise if infection is present.
Tests confirm infection, assess nutrition, and evaluate systemic status. Use available resources and interpret results in context.
